title: Devlog framework, browser, dev tool, dictation and command palette
summary: Set up a documentation framework for every project in `D:\Game Dev`: a `devlog` skill that turns each Claude session into an HTML report and keeps per-project agent memory, enforced by a Stop hook. Then built `devlog/browse.html` (dark, every project, feature groups), made it a dev tool (`Start-Devlog.bat`: status, launching and following Claude sessions), added local Whisper dictation, and replaced the search box with a command palette that does everything by typing or by voice.

decisions.title: Where do the logs and memory live?
decisions.choice: A `devlog/` folder inside each project (Workspace, Forge, Extraction Game), same shape everywhere, plus a cross-project home page.
decisions.why: Travels with each repo, readable by any agent and by Jon; Claude's per-user memory folder is invisible to both.
alternatives: One central folder for all projects

decisions.title: What is the source of truth?
decisions.choice: `session.json` and markdown; HTML pages and `WORKLOG.md` are generated by `devlog.py render`.
decisions.why: Agents edit structured data reliably; pages can change style without rewriting history; the worklog can be rebuilt commit by commit.

decisions.title: How is the prompt captured?
decisions.choice: Extracted verbatim from the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/*/<session>.jsonl`), along with later messages, AskUserQuestion answers, model, times and edited files; commits from `git log`.
decisions.why: The user asked for the prompt that started the work; an agent's recollection drifts, especially after context compaction.

decisions.title: How is "always at the end of their work" enforced?
decisions.choice: A Stop hook in the user settings that blocks the first stop of a session that edited workspace files without an up-to-date log, plus the rule in `D:\Game Dev\CLAUDE.md`.
decisions.why: A rule alone is easy to skip at the end of a long session. User-level so it also fires for sessions started inside `Forge\` or a game folder; it does nothing outside `D:\Game Dev`, and `devlog.py skip` is the escape hatch.
alternatives: Project-level hook (would miss sessions started in sub-projects)

decisions.title: How are screenshots and video taken?
decisions.choice: Scripts that write files: `capture.ps1` (any window, .NET), `record.ps1` (ffmpeg gdigrab, also converts Godot/Playwright clips), `capture_web.mjs` (Playwright with installed Edge, scripted steps, video, or attach over CDP to the real WebView2).
decisions.why: The built-in screenshot tools return images to the agent but save nothing.

decisions.title: Backfill Forge?
decisions.choice: Yes: overview, handoff, a feature file per slice (0 to 3 detailed from the docs and perf log, 4 to 9 as planned stubs), and a session log for slice 3 built from its transcript.
decisions.why: An empty corpus gives the next agent nothing; Forge already had plans, a perf log and a transcript to draw on. The backfilled session is marked as such.

decisions.title: Install ffmpeg now?
decisions.choice: Installed on request: ffmpeg 9.0.2 via winget (`Gyan.FFmpeg`) and Playwright's ffmpeg build.
decisions.why: Window recording (`record.ps1`) and web-page video (`capture_web.mjs --video`) both need it.

decisions.title: How does the browser know which pages exist?
decisions.choice: `devlog.py render` writes `devlog/browse.html` with a manifest of every project, session, feature and media file embedded as JSON.
decisions.why: Pages open from `file://`, where a page cannot list folders or fetch files. Raw HTML/CSS/JS, no build step or framework, as asked.
alternatives: A local web server with a directory API

decisions.title: How does the sidebar follow links clicked inside a page?
decisions.choice: Every generated page posts its address to the parent window when it is framed; the browser maps it back to the manifest and updates the address and the highlight.
decisions.why: Browsers treat `file://` frames as cross-origin, so the parent cannot read the frame's location. postMessage works across that boundary. The same channel forwards the j, k and / shortcuts pressed while the page has focus.

decisions.title: Light or dark?
decisions.choice: Dark by default on every page; light only behind an explicit `data-theme=light`. Saved as a standing preference for all future designs.
decisions.why: "make it dark mode. Always default to dark mode designs"

decisions.title: Which projects does the browser show?
decisions.choice: Every folder under `D:\Game Dev` that has a `devlog/`, searched up to 4 levels deep, skipping engine installs, ComfyUI, build output, dependencies and engine caches. Nested projects are named by path (`Games/Foo`).
decisions.why: "the main browser needs to show the devlogs for all projects in the game dev folder if a devlog exists". The scan takes ~0.1 s.

decisions.title: How are features grouped (e.g. several slices under one feature)?
decisions.choice: Front matter in the feature file: `parent: <slug>` names the group feature, `order: <n>` sorts siblings. A group is an ordinary feature file; its status and "2/4 done" roll up from its members. Groups nest.
decisions.why: Links to `features/<slug>.md` from sessions, WORKLOG and other features keep working, and regrouping is one line (`devlog.py feature ... --parent`). A group keeps its own notes and decisions.
alternatives: Folders (`features/<group>/<slice>.md`): would break existing links and make slugs ambiguous

decisions.title: How to group Forge's ten slices?
decisions.choice: Generation engine (slices 0, 2, 3, 9), 3D models and export (1, 7), Asset stages: map to asset images (4, 5, 6); Voice (8) stays on its own.
decisions.why: Follows what each slice builds rather than release order: shared crates and shared budgets. Easy to change with `--parent`.

decisions.title: How can the browser change status and start Claude?
decisions.choice: A local server, `devlog_server.py` (Python standard library), started by `Start-Devlog.bat`, serving the same pages plus an API. The `file://` version stays as a read-only fallback.
decisions.why: A page opened from disk cannot write files or start processes.

decisions.title: How is the server kept safe?
decisions.choice: 127.0.0.1 only; Host header must be 127.0.0.1/localhost; a random token per server start, written into the served page, required on every API call; Origin checked; static files limited to the workspace, no dot-folders, an extension allowlist; `bypassPermissions` never offered.
decisions.why: It can start Claude sessions, so other websites (CSRF, DNS rebinding) and other files must not be able to drive or read it.

decisions.title: How are sessions launched?
decisions.choice: The Claude Code CLI bundled with the desktop app. Terminal mode opens a console that runs the session with a pre-assigned session id and records how it ended; background mode uses `claude --bg`. Status for both comes from `claude agents --json`.
decisions.why: No standalone `claude` on PATH; the bundled one is the same Claude Code and has `--bg`, `agents`, `attach`, `stop`.

decisions.title: Log the CLI in from the tool?
decisions.choice: No: the tool shows a banner and opens `claude auth login` in a terminal; the user signs in there.
decisions.why: Signing in is the user's to do; the server never handles credentials.

decisions.title: Which speech-to-text engine, and where can you dictate?
decisions.choice: Local Whisper (faster-whisper, large-v3-turbo) on this PC; dictation in launch prompts, the search box, and voice notes saved into the devlog.
decisions.why: Private and offline, better with code and game terms, and the RTX 5080 makes it near-instant.
alternatives: Browser speech recognition (no install, live text, but audio goes to Microsoft/Google)

decisions.title: How should spoken commands be understood?
decisions.choice: A local intent parser in the page: phrase patterns plus fuzzy name matching ("slice four", bare names, slugs), with anything unplaced offered as "Ask Claude" or "Capture as an idea".
decisions.why: Instant, works offline and without the CLI login, and predictable about what it will do.
alternatives: Send every command to Claude to interpret (slower, needs login, less predictable)

decisions.title: What may a spoken command do without confirmation?
decisions.choice: Only navigation where every name was understood runs by itself; anything that changes files or starts a session is highlighted and waits for Enter.
decisions.why: A mis-heard command should never change the devlog or launch Claude. A test where Whisper heard the phrase twice auto-navigated to the wrong project before this rule.

decisions.title: Where does the skill live now that the devlog has its own repo?
decisions.choice: In the repo as `devlog\skill\`, linked into `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\devlog`; `devlog.py install` sets up the link and the Stop hook on any PC.
decisions.why: Jon wanted the devlog project and the skill in one repo. A visible `skill/` folder keeps the tool and the workspace's own log side by side; the user-level link keeps the skill available from every project folder.
alternatives: `devlog/.claude/skills/devlog` (only picked up when Claude starts inside the devlog folder)

timeline.text: Surveyed the workspace: Forge (Rust/Tauri + React, slices 0 to 3, plans in `docs/`), an empty Extraction Game repo, Pipeline and Setup. No existing CLAUDE.md, skills or user settings.
Transcripts carry `origin.kind = human` on the user's own messages, `custom-title`, `file-history-delta` entries and the model id, which is enough to extract the prompt and follow-ups exactly.
Wrote `devlog.py` (stdlib only): init, start, media, feature, render, where, skip, hook; a small markdown renderer; session, project and home pages; WORKLOG generation.
The workspace project's page and the cross-project home both wanted `devlog/index.html`.
The workspace project's page became `devlog/workspace.html`; all links are computed with relative paths.

Wrote the skill (`SKILL.md`, session schema, capture recipes for Forge, Godot, Unreal), templates, `devlog/GUIDE.md` and the root `CLAUDE.md`; linked the skill into the user skills folder with a junction; added the Stop hook.
Hook checked against three real transcripts: blocks a session with edits and no log, allows with `stop_hook_active`, allows outside the workspace.
The slice 3 session wrote most files through Bash, so only 22 of 57 changed files were detected.
`render` now also adds uncommitted files modified during the session window (57 detected).
Backfilled Forge and rendered the slice 3 session page.
Project page: features ordered in progress, done, planned; features with no sessions collapsed; relative links in inlined plans fixed; feature titles prefixed with their slice number.
Logged this session with the skill itself.
Installed ffmpeg (winget) and Playwright's ffmpeg. Verified a 3 s H.264 window recording, a web-page video, and webm to mp4 conversion.

Built `browse.html`: sidebar with projects (sessions and features per project), a timeline tab, a media gallery with filters, full-text search over titles, summaries, prompts, decisions and timelines, Older/Newer buttons and j/k keys, deep links (`browse.html#/<page>`), and a mobile layout. Each page got a "Browse all" link back into it.
The in-app browser pane shows `file://` pages as static snapshots without scripts, so it could not test the browser.
Tested in real Edge through Playwright instead: navigation, links inside pages, search, deep links, mobile width, no console errors.
j/k did nothing after clicking inside a page: the keystrokes went to the framed page.
Framed pages forward j, k and / to the browser.
Switched every page and the browser to dark by default, at your request.
Summaries on index pages were cut mid-word ("*Backfil"); they now end at a word boundary without a dangling emphasis marker.
Project discovery now searches every folder up to 4 levels deep. Tested with a temporary nested project and a bare `devlog/` folder: both appeared in the sidebar and opened, then were deleted.
Scripting a scroll inside a framed `file://` page is blocked (cross-origin).
Added a `wheel` step to `capture_web.mjs` that scrolls whatever is under the mouse, frames included, and recorded a tour of the browser.

Added feature groups: `feature_tree()` nests features by `parent:`, sorts by `order:`, rolls status up, and ignores unknown parents and cycles. `devlog.py feature` gained `--parent` and `--order` (also regroups existing files).

Project page: group cards list their members with status and progress; the build history shows each group's sessions labelled by member, with each member collapsible below. Links to a member open its section.
Browser sidebar: groups are collapsible nodes showing "n/m done"; a chevron toggles, the name opens the group, and opening a member expands its group.
Grouped Forge's slices under three new group features.
No `claude` on PATH, but the desktop app bundles Claude Code 2.1.295 with `--session-id`, `--bg`, `agents --json`, `attach`, `logs`, `stop`, `--permission-mode` and `--remote-control`.

Wrote `devlog_server.py`: static serving with range requests, `/api/state`, feature status, run/resume, run activity from the transcript, stop/attach, login, render. `devlog.py serve` and `Start-Devlog.bat` start it.
Security probes: no token 403, foreign Host 421, cross-origin POST 403, traversal 403, dot-folders and scripts 403; pages, docs and video (206) served.

Browser: header status dropdown and ▶ Run in Claude on features, Resume on sessions, New session on projects; right-click menu on sidebar features; a launch dialog with an editable generated prompt, terminal or background, permission mode, Remote Control, mark in progress; a Runs tab with live state and recent activity.
Changed Voice and Slice 4 status through the dropdown and the right-click menu: files, sidebar, group rollup and the framed page all updated; restored both.
A background test launch answered "Not logged in", and `--bg` ignored the pre-assigned session id.

The server now reads the real session id from `--bg` output and `agents --json`, reports `claude auth status`, shows a login banner with a button that opens `claude auth login`, disables Start while logged out, and marks runs that hit it as failed with an explanation.

Terminal launch on Forge Voice opened a Windows Terminal window titled with the feature in the Forge folder; Stop closed it. Background launch resolved its session, showed its activity, and stopped. Test run records removed afterwards.
Installed faster-whisper with NVIDIA cuBLAS/cuDNN wheels; ctranslate2 sees the RTX 5080. Wrote `devlog_stt.py` (lazy load, GPU with CPU fallback, idle unload, vocabulary hint).
faster-whisper 1.2.1 failed with PyAV 19 (`metadata_errors`).
Pinned PyAV 16.0.1. First run downloaded the model (~21 s); warm, 13 s of speech transcribes in 0.24 s on the GPU.

Server: `/api/transcribe` (raw audio), `/api/stt/warm`, `/api/note`. Browser: mic buttons with a level ring and timer on the launch prompt, search and the note dialog; Alt+M toggles, Esc discards; a Note/Idea button on features and projects that opens straight into recording; "Add a note…" in the right-click menu.

The hint now keeps only the distinctive words of feature names; three repeat runs came back word-perfect in 0.22 s.

Server: create a feature, read and write its description, move it between groups, open a project in Explorer or VS Code, prompts for brainstorm, describe and plan sessions; HANDOFF next steps in the manifest.

Browser: the sidebar search became the palette (Ctrl+K, `/`, start typing, or Alt+M to speak). Empty, it shows actions for the current page, the project's next steps and every command; typed or spoken, it shows best matches, matching commands, pages that mention the words, and Ask Claude / Capture as idea.
Describe dialog for a feature's summary and "What it is", with mics and a "Work it out with Claude" button; creating a feature opens it straight away.
27 example phrases checked: 26 right first time; "start ideation" produced the topic "tion".
Regex alternatives ordered longest first with word boundaries; duplicate Ask Claude fallback removed.

End to end in Edge: created a feature and saved its description, set statuses by phrase and through the step-by-step flow, moved and ungrouped a feature, opened a brainstorm prompt. All changes reverted.
Spoken "go to the Forge handoff" (heard twice because the test recorded past the clip) fell back to the alphabetically first project and navigated there by itself.
Auto-run only when every name resolved; the fallback project is now the one worked on most recently. Re-run: navigation went to Forge's handoff; "mark slice 4 in progress" waited for Enter.

Moved the skill into the devlog repo as `skill/`, re-pointed the user-level link and the Stop hook, and updated every path reference (CLAUDE.md, Start-Devlog.bat, GUIDE, OVERVIEW, SKILL.md, capture recipes).
The hook's corpus check treated anything under a `devlog` folder as logging; it now excludes the skill folder, so editing the tool still counts as work.
Added `devlog.py install` (link plus hook, idempotent, updates an older path), a `.gitignore` for machine-local state, and a README for the repo.
From the new location: install reported both already correct, render, the Stop hook, the server, the palette and dictation all work; scripts are not served over HTTP.

For human review, for each session, you should generate an HTML page that documents the prompt that was used to start this work, decisions that were made along the way, about what to do, take screenshots and videos of new features as they are added, uh, and document as well as you can the development process of each feature.

This skill should always be used at agents at the end of their work. This applies to sub-projects within game dev, such as Forge or any games that are worked on.
